pattern: Of the 15 wrong runs, 10 (Chart-1 and CHART-1-L10-SECONDARY-02, runs 001-005) are provider_not_configured. They have no trajectory and no predictions, so they are infrastructure exclusions, not model failures. The other 5 are all variants of the same one-line Closure-1 fault: the `!removeGlobals && !modifyCallSites` guard, in L10, L50 x2, NAME-L10 and NAME-L50. They fail the same way. Every run ranks the downstream executor CallSiteOptimizer.markUnreferencedFunctionArgs 1st and the upstream policy gate 2nd or 3rd. In all 5 runs the agent fully displayed the gold guard with its issue-253 comment and reproduced the test. All 5 also had the Expected/Result diff in the prompt and retrieved DefaultPassConfig's optimizeCalls wiring; 4 of 5 also read the CompilerOptions LOCAL_ONLY setter. Two runs (L10 run-001 and NAME-L10) wrote the correct causal diagnosis into their evidence_chain (gate bypassed under LOCAL_ONLY+optimizeCalls) and still ranked the executor first. The other three never connected removeGlobals=false to the gate. Every evidence_chain blames the decoy's correct `modifyAllCallSites || !hasFollowing` trailing-parameter fallback as 'bypassing' canChangeSignature's rejection of the .length use. The failure is therefore a local-oddness / proximate-executor bias, not a search, retrieval or lexical failure. The name ablation is irrelevant, since the non-ablated L10 and L50 fail identically. Two instance annotations conflict with the trajectories: L10 run-001 did read the DefaultPassConfig/CompilerOptions option mapping, and NAME-L50 did read the DefaultPassConfig `!removeOnlyLocals` wiring.
